title: Finite cohomological dimension bounds the unbounded derived functor from above
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], and suppose $\mathcal A$ has enough injectives, meaning every object embeds in an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive and left exact, with right derived functors $R^qF$ on objects [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Fix an integer $N\geq0$ and assume $R^qF(A)=0$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$ and every $q>N$. Use unbounded cochain derived categories and their cohomology functors [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then the total right derived functor $RF:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ exists. For every integer $t$ and every $E\in D(\mathcal A)$ with $H^i(E)=0$ for all $i>t$, one has $H^i(RF(E))=0$ for all $i>t+N$.

proof.text: Define d(X) to be the least natural number n such that R^qF(X)=0 for all q>n. It exists and is at most D=N.toNat. Injective vanishing [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-injective-vanishing] makes d of an injective zero and supplies degree-zero embeddings. Additivity of R^qF and preservation of binary biproducts give the maximum inequality on sums. For a short exact sequence S, apply the exact segment R^qF(S.X2) -> R^qF(S.X3) -> R^(q+1)F(S.X1) of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact]. Both outer terms vanish for q>max(d(S.X1)-1,d(S.X2)), so the least-bound property gives the required cokernel inequality. This is the private helper exists_rightAcyclic_replacement.

source.place: Tag 07K7, lemma-unbounded-right-derived, second proof paragraph: degree function and verification of the hypotheses of 07K6.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-degree-zero-complex-replacement] to the degree function verified in Step 1. If d(L^r)=0, its defining bound gives R^(q+1)F(L^r)=0 for every natural q. Hence every complex admits a quasi-isomorphism into a termwise right-F-acyclic complex, with no bound on its cochain degrees.

proof.text: Use Functor.quasiIso_map_of_rightAcyclic_of_isZero_rightDerived from the same source module. Its proved cone argument applies Step 3, closure of right-F-acyclic objects under biproducts, and [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] on both sides. Thus F sends quasi-isomorphisms between termwise right-F-acyclic complexes to quasi-isomorphisms. On the homotopy category, lift an arbitrary arrow through the full quotient functor; the quotient quasi-isomorphism criterion and localization then give invertibility of its image.

source.place: Tag 05RT, lemma-acyclic, and Tag 07K7, quasi-isomorphism preservation claim.

proof.text: Let G=F.mapHomotopyCategory followed by Qh for B; Mathlib supplies commutation with shifts and triangulatedness [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]. Use the class of complexes whose terms are right-F-acyclic. Steps 2 and 4 verify the replacement and inversion hypotheses of [lem-sf-right-derived-from-adapted-complexes], producing RF, alpha_h and invertibility of alpha_h on this class. The factorization of termwise F followed by Q through the homotopy quotient is a natural isomorphism. Precomposition by that quotient is fully faithful, so the inverse factorization is a left Kan extension (proved as private helper isLeftKanExtension_of_full_whiskering). Compose the two Kan extensions with Mathlib Functor.isLeftKanExtension_iff_postcompose and the isomorphism quotientCompQhIso. This proves the exact cochain-localization universal property in the statement.

source.place: Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes, applied as in the proof of 07K7 (1)-(2).

proof.text: Choose an acyclic replacement L of a representative of E, giving E isomorphic to Q(L). The homology factorization transfers the upper bound t to exactness of L above t. For n>=t, exactness at n+1 gives the short exact sequence of cycles. The long exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] and acyclicity of L^(n-1) make its connecting map R^(q+1)F(Z^n) -> R^(q+2)F(Z^(n-1)) monic. Induct on k: when n>=t+k and D<=q+k, R^(q+1)F(Z^n)=0. At k=0 use the uniform vanishing bound; at k+1 use this monomorphism and the induction hypothesis at n-1,q+1. Taking k=D shows Z^n is F-acyclic for n>=t+D. Thus F preserves the short exact cycles sequence at n>=t+D (map_of_rightAcyclic, using R^0F=F from [lem-sp-derived-well-defined]). Preservation of kernels and the resulting epimorphism F(L^n)->F(Z^(n+1)) prove F(L) exact at n+1. This is private helper map_rightAcyclic_upper_bound and covers D=0 without a separate case. Invertibility of alpha_h at L, the explicit comparison alpha, and homologyFunctorFactors transfer this bound to RF(E).
